concepts.name: Five pure vowel sounds
concepts.summary: Recall and pronounce the five Spanish vowels a, e, i, o, u as consistent, short, unreduced sounds.

concepts.name: Core greetings and farewells
concepts.summary: Recall and use common greetings, farewells and polite formulas such as hola, buenos días, por favor and gracias.

concepts.name: Noun gender and articles
concepts.summary: Understand that nouns are masculine or feminine and match el/la and un/una, using endings -o and -a as a guide.

concepts.name: Plural formation and agreement
concepts.summary: Form plurals with -s or -es and understand that adjectives agree with nouns in gender and number.

concepts.name: Subject pronouns and tú/usted
concepts.summary: Recognise subject pronouns and explain when to use informal tú versus formal usted.

concepts.name: Present tense of ser
concepts.summary: Understand and use present forms of ser to state identity, origin and basic characteristics.

concepts.name: Basic food ordering phrases
concepts.summary: Understand and produce simple phrases for ordering food and drink, such as quisiera, me gustaría and la cuenta, por favor.

misconceptions.text: Spanish vowels change quality depending on stress or position, as in English.
All nouns ending in -a are feminine and all ending in -o are masculine.
Subject pronouns must always be used in every sentence, as in English.

concepts.name: Estar for location and state
concepts.summary: Use estar for location and temporary conditions such as feelings and states.

concepts.name: Ser versus estar contrast
concepts.summary: Choose between ser and estar in common sentences by applying the rules of identity and characteristics versus location and state.

concepts.name: Regular present tense conjugation
concepts.summary: Conjugate regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the present tense for all persons.

concepts.name: Tener idioms
concepts.summary: Use tener expressions such as tener hambre, sed, frío, miedo and years of age where English uses to be.

concepts.name: Hacer weather expressions
concepts.summary: Use hacer in weather expressions such as hace calor and hace viento and in the verb's basic meaning to do or make.

concepts.name: Rolled r and single r
concepts.summary: Distinguish and produce the single tap r and the trilled rr, noting how it changes meaning in pairs like pero and perro.

concepts.name: Travel and direction phrases
concepts.summary: Apply phrases to ask for directions, buy tickets and book accommodation.

concepts.name: Stem-changing present verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate common stem-changing verbs such as querer, poder and dormir in the present tense.

misconceptions.text: Ser is for permanent things and estar for temporary ones, with no exceptions.
Tener expressions translate literally as to be, so I am hungry becomes soy hambre.
Stem changes apply to every verb form, including nosotros and vosotros.

concepts.name: Regular preterite formation
concepts.summary: Form and use the preterite of regular verbs to narrate completed past actions.

concepts.name: Irregular preterite verbs
concepts.summary: Apply irregular preterite forms of common verbs such as ir, ser, hacer, tener and estar.

concepts.name: Imperfect tense formation
concepts.summary: Form the imperfect, including the irregular ser, ir and ver, for habitual and ongoing past actions.

concepts.name: Preterite versus imperfect
concepts.summary: Analyse a narrative to decide between completed events and background, habitual or ongoing states.

concepts.name: Object and reflexive pronouns
concepts.summary: Place direct, indirect and reflexive pronouns correctly, including se lo and pronoun attachment.

concepts.name: Gustar-type verbs
concepts.summary: Use gustar-type verbs with indirect objects and agreement with the thing liked.

concepts.name: Por versus para
concepts.summary: Distinguish uses of por and para by analysing purpose, cause, duration and destination.

concepts.name: Latin American and Castilian differences
concepts.summary: Compare major regional features such as vosotros versus ustedes, seseo versus distinción, and vocabulary differences like coche and carro.

misconceptions.text: The preterite is just the simple past and the imperfect is just used to say used to.
Gustar agrees with the person who likes something, so I like apples is me gusto manzanas.
Spanish in Latin America is a simplified or incorrect version of Castilian Spanish.

concepts.name: Present subjunctive formation
concepts.summary: Form the present subjunctive of regular, stem-changing and irregular verbs by analysing the yo-form stem.

concepts.name: Subjunctive with wishes and emotion
concepts.summary: Analyse triggers of volition, emotion, doubt and denial that require subjunctive in subordinate clauses with a change of subject.

concepts.name: Subjunctive in adverbial clauses
concepts.summary: Distinguish when conjunctions like cuando, aunque and antes de que take indicative or subjunctive.

concepts.name: Imperfect subjunctive and si-clauses
concepts.summary: Form the imperfect subjunctive and use it in contrary-to-fact si-clauses with the conditional.

concepts.name: Perfect and compound tenses
concepts.summary: Analyse the use of haber with participles, including regional preference for present perfect versus preterite.

concepts.name: Commands and formal register
concepts.summary: Form affirmative and negative commands for tú, usted and ustedes and choose appropriate register.

concepts.name: Voseo and regional pronoun systems
concepts.summary: Evaluate how voseo, ustedes-for-vosotros and leísmo shape appropriate usage across regions.

misconceptions.text: The subjunctive is a tense that refers to uncertain future time.
Voseo is substandard slang used only by uneducated speakers.

concepts.name: Mood choice as speaker stance
concepts.summary: Evaluate how indicative and subjunctive choices express speaker stance, assertion and presupposition beyond rules.

concepts.name: Register and dialect adaptation
concepts.summary: Adapt vocabulary, pronouns, pronunciation and idioms to suit audience and region in speech and writing.

concepts.name: Pragmatics of politeness and indirection
concepts.summary: Evaluate conditional, imperfect and diminutive strategies for politeness and tone across cultures.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and figurative expression
concepts.summary: Create natural idiomatic phrasing using expressions with tener, hacer, dar and echar, and recognise regional variants.

concepts.name: Discourse cohesion in extended text
concepts.summary: Compose coherent extended texts using connectors, tense sequencing, and clitic and ellipsis choices.

concepts.name: Critiquing usage norms
concepts.summary: Evaluate prescriptive norms from the RAE and ASALE against actual usage and justify choices in context.

misconceptions.text: Native-like Spanish means following one standard variety, usually Castilian.
Mood choice is a mechanical rule following triggers, not a meaningful choice.
Translating English idioms word for word yields natural Spanish.
